37573-pencil-sketches-or-outlines-of-cha.title: Pencil Sketches Or Outlines Of Character And Manners
37573-pencil-sketches-or-outlines-of-cha.creator: Unknown
37573-pencil-sketches-or-outlines-of-cha.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Bromley Cheston, an officer in the United States navy, had just returned from a three years' cruise in the Mediterranean. His ship came into New York; and after he had spent a week with a sister that was married in Boston, he could not resist his inclination to pay a visit to his maternal aunt, who had resided since her widowhood at one of the small towns on the banks of the Delaware.

arxiv-1805-06474.title: Understanding Federation: An Analytical Framework for the Interoperability of Social Networking Sites
arxiv-1805-06474.creator: Antonio Tapiador, Samer Hassan
arxiv-1805-06474.description: Abstract Although social networking has become a remarkable feature in the Web, full interoperability has not arrived. This work explores the main 5 paradigms of interoperability across social networking sites, corresponding to the layers in which we can find interoperability. Building on those, a novel analytical framework for SNS interoperability is introduced.

arxiv-2012-15066.title: The rank of universal m m -gonal forms
arxiv-2012-15066.creator: Byeong Moon Kim and Dayoon Park
arxiv-2012-15066.description: Abstract . In this article, we consider the rank of universal m m -gonal forms for all sufficiently large m m . Especially, we determine the minimal rank of universal m m -gonal form and the maximal rank of kinds of proper universal m m -gonal form. 1.

arxiv-2109-11517.title: Nordic vaccination strategies face/off via age range comparative analysis on key indicators of COVID-19 severity and healthcare stress level
arxiv-2109-11517.creator: Anna Sigridur Islind, María Óskarsdóttir, Corentin Cot, Giacomo Cacciapaglia, Francesco Sannino
arxiv-2109-11517.description: Abstract In this paper we analyze the impact of vaccinations on spread of the COVID-19 virus for different age groups. More specifically we examine the deployment of vaccines in the Nordic countries in a comparative analysis where we analyze factors such as healthcare stress level and severity of disease through new infections, hospitalizations, intensive care unit (ICU) occupancy and deaths.

arxiv-2211-08810.title: On projective representations of Plesken Lie algebras
arxiv-2211-08810.creator: P G Romeo, Arjun S N
arxiv-2211-08810.description: Abstract In this article we describe the projective representation of Plesken Lie algebras and equivalent central extensions of the same. Further it is also shown that there exists a bijective correspondence between second cohomology group, equivalent central extensions and projectively equivalent projective representations of Plesken Lie algebras.

arxiv-2212-11161.title: Josephson effect in excitonic chiral double layers
arxiv-2212-11161.creator: Klaus Ziegler
arxiv-2212-11161.description: Abstract Considering s-wave pairing in an electron-hole double layer of two chiral metals, we study the Josephson effect generated by a domain wall. The latter, which is caused by a jump of the order parameter phase, creates two independent evanescent zero-energy modes at an exceptional point.

arxiv-2306-02707.title: Orca: Progressive Learning from Complex Explanation Traces of GPT-4
arxiv-2306-02707.creator: Subhabrata Mukherjee, Arindam Mitra
arxiv-2306-02707.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Subhabrata Mukherjee, Arindam Mitra. Recent research has focused on enhancing the capability of smaller models through imitation learning, drawing on the outputs generated by large foundation models (LFMs). A number of issues impact the quality of these models, ranging from limited imitation signals from shallow LFM outputs; small scale homogeneous training data; and most notably a lack of rigorous evaluation resulting in overestimating the small model’s capability as they tend to learn to imitate the style, but not the reasoning process of LFMs .

arxiv-2307-16123.title: Exploiting Parallel Memory Write Requests for Covert Channel Attacks in Integrated CPU-GPU Systems
arxiv-2307-16123.creator: Ghadeer Almusaddar galmusa1@binghamton.edu Binghamton University, Hoda Naghibijouybari hnaghibi@binghamton.edu Binghamton University
arxiv-2307-16123.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ghadeer Almusaddar galmusa1@binghamton.edu Binghamton University, Hoda Naghibijouybari hnaghibi@binghamton.edu Binghamton University. In heterogeneous SoCs, accelerators like integrated GPUs (iGPUs) are integrated on the same chip as CPUs, sharing the memory subsystem. In such systems, the massive memory requests from throughput-oriented accelerators significantly interfere with CPU memory requests. In addition to the large performance impact, this interference provides an attacker with a strong leakage vector for covert attacks across the processors, which is hard to achieve across the cores in a multi-core CPU.

arxiv-2401-13240.title: A pilot search for MeV gamma-ray emission from five galaxy clusters using archival COMPTEL data
arxiv-2401-13240.creator: Siddhant Manna, Shantanu Desai
arxiv-2401-13240.description: Abstract We search for MeV gamma-ray emission between 0.75-30 MeV from five galaxy clusters, viz. Coma, VIRGO, SPT-CL J2012-5649, Bullet, and El Gordo, using archival data from the COMPTEL telescope. For this purpose we use three search templates: point source, radial disk and radial Gaussian.

arxiv-2502-20598.title: Scalable Coordinated Learning for H2M/R Applications over Optical Access Networks (Invited)
arxiv-2502-20598.creator: Sourav Mondal and Elaine Wong
arxiv-2502-20598.description: Abstract One of the primary research interests adhering to next-generation fiber-wireless access networks is human-to-machine/robot (H2M/R) collaborative communications facilitating Industry 5.0. This paper discusses scalable H2M/R communications across large geographical distances that also allow rapid onboarding of new machines/robots as ∼ 72 % \sim 72\% training time is saved through global-local coordinated learning.

arxiv-2505-04436.title: Nearly spanning cycle in the percolated hypercube
arxiv-2505-04436.creator: Michael Anastos, Sahar Diskin, Joshua Erde, Mihyun Kang, Michael Krivelevich, Lyuben Lichev
arxiv-2505-04436.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Michael Anastos, Sahar Diskin, Joshua Erde, Mihyun Kang, Michael Krivelevich, Lyuben Lichev. Let Q d Q^{d} be the d d -dimensional binary hypercube. We form a random subgraph Q p d ⊆ Q d Q^{d}_{p}\subseteq Q^{d} by retaining each edge of Q d Q^{d} independently with probability p p .

arxiv-2512-24207.title: Notes on the LVP and the CVP in
arxiv-2512-24207.creator: p
arxiv-2512-24207.description: Abstract Abstract This paper explores computational methods for solving the Longest Vector Problem (LVP) and Closest Vector Problem (CVP) in p -adic fields. Leveraging the non-Archimedean property of p -adic norms, we propose a polynomial time algorithm to compute orthogonal bases for p -adic lattices when the p -adic field is given by a minimal polynomial.

arxiv-2602-11188.title: Radiating solutions in Entangled Relativity
arxiv-2602-11188.creator: Olivier Minazzoli, Maxime Wavasseur
arxiv-2602-11188.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Olivier Minazzoli, Maxime Wavasseur. The Mineur–Vaidya radiating solutions satisfy ℒ m ∝ F 2 = 0 = R \mathcal{L}_{m}~\propto~F^{2}=0=R . As a consequence, it is not only a solution in General Relativity, but also in Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton theories for all coupling constants. The specific case of Entangled Relativity is noteworthy because the additional scalar degree of freedom is defined from the ratio between R R and ℒ m \mathcal{L}_{m} , which is ill-defined in this situation.

pmc-11426327.title: Decoding the molecular symphony: interactions between the m6A and p53 signaling pathways in cancer
pmc-11426327.creator: Rachel Shoemaker, Mo-Fan Huang, Ying-Si Wu, Cheng-Shuo Huang, Dung-Fang Lee
pmc-11426327.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The p53 tumor suppressor gene governs a multitude of complex cellular processes that are essential for anti-cancer function and whose dysregulation leads to aberrant gene transcription, activation of oncogenic signaling and cancer development. Although mutations can occur at any point in the genetic sequence, missense mutations comprise the majority of observed p53 mutations in cancers regardless of whether the mutation is germline or somatic.

pmc-11486646.title: Effect of forest cover on lung cancer incidence: a case study in Southwest China
pmc-11486646.creator: Haishi Yu, Yang Wang, Jinyu Huang, Xiaoli Yue, Jun Chu, Guiquan Sun, Han Gao, Min Yang, Hong’ou Zhang
pmc-11486646.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionForests are closely linked to human health, particularly about lung cancer incidence. However, there is currently limited research on how forest coverage and different types of forests influence lung cancer rates. This study aims to address this gap by examining how the coverage of various forest types impacts lung cancer incidence in Southwest China, thereby providing theoretical support for health-oriented forest structure planning.MethodsWe focused on 438 counties in Southwest China, employing spatial autocorrelation analysis (Moran’s I) and spatial regression models [including Spatial

pmc-11550620.title: High-fat-diet-induced hepatic insulin resistance per se attenuates murine de novo lipogenesis
pmc-11550620.creator: Leigh Goedeke, Jordan W Strober, Rebecca Suh, Lauren M Paolella, Xiruo Li, Jillian C Rogers, Max C Petersen, Ali R Nasiri, Gregori Casals, Mario Kahn, Gary W Cline, Varman T Samuel, Gerald I Shulman, Daniel F Vatner
pmc-11550620.description: SummaryHepatic insulin resistance (IR) is often said to be “pathway-selective” with preserved insulin stimulation of de novo lipogenesis (DNL) despite attenuated insulin signaling toward glucose metabolism. However, DNL has not been assessed in models of liver-specific IR. We studied mice with differential tissue-specific lipid-induced IR achieved by different durations of high-fat diet (HFD) feeding.

pmc-11688798.title: MITOCHONDRIA, METABOLISM, AND GLUTATHIONE AS MEDIATORS OF COGNITIVE DECLINE IN AGING AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE
pmc-11688798.creator: Rajagopal Sekhar, George Taffet
pmc-11688798.description: Aging is the most important risk factor for cognitive decline and Alzheimer’s disease (AD), and age-related cognitive decline (ACD) is widely prevalent in older adults (OA). However, the mechanistic underpinnings of cognitive impairment in aging and AD remain poorly understood, and are a high-priority research focus toward finding solutions.

pmc-12604379.title: Oxidative stress and fertility studies of selected plants using female Drosophila melanogaster
pmc-12604379.creator: H. O. Alaka, T. O. Ajayi, A. O. Abolaji
pmc-12604379.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveLow-to-moderate oxidative stress (OS) plays physiological roles in reproduction. However, excessive production of OS markers has been implicated in infertility, and the use of medicinal plants for its management is based on a paucity of scientific confirmation.

pmc-12621491.title: Design and construction of nanoengineered multifunctional microneedles with sustained-release properties for targeted microenvironment remodeling in diabetic bone regeneration
pmc-12621491.creator: Heyi Gong, Sihan Ma, Boyuan Wang, Yue Liu, Xiao Han, Yu Wang, Duo Sun, Yadi Su, Junqi Wang, Jinghui Zhao
pmc-12621491.description: Chronic periodontitis associated with diabetes mellitus (CPDM) presents significant challenges due to an impaired tissue microenvironment characterized by persistent oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and dysfunction of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). Nanotechnology-driven Met@ZIF-8@PDA microneedle (MN) therapeutic platform has been developed that integrates multiple functions and allows for precise modulation.

pmc-12641750.title: Associations Between Neurofeedback, Anthropometrics, Technical, Physical, and Tactical Performance in Young Women’s Football Players
pmc-12641750.creator: Sílvio A. Carvalho, Pedro Bezerra, José E. Teixeira, Pedro Forte, Rui M. Silva, José Mª Cancela-Carral
pmc-12641750.description: Background: Neurofeedback training has emerged as a promising tool for enhancing performance by targeting specific brain activity patterns linked to motor skills, decision-making, and concentration. This study aimed to explore the associations between neurofeedback outcomes and football-specific performance metrics, including anthropometric, physical, technical, and tactical dimensions.

pmc-12705124.title: Uveal Melanocytoma without GNAQ/GNA11 Mutations
pmc-12705124.creator: Seth T. Kazmer, Rachel Frauches, Carlo Galang, Marinia Bishay, Don S. Minckler, Prithvi Mruthyunjaya, Jonathan H. Lin
pmc-12705124.description: IntroductionUveal melanocytomas are benign melanocytic proliferations characterized histologically by large polyhedral cells, abundant intracytoplasmic melanin, small centrally located nuclei, and low nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios (N:C). Activating missense changes of the G-protein subunits, GNAQ/GNA11, drive uveal melanocytic proliferation and are characteristic molecular mutations found in intraocular nevi including melanocytomas, as well as malignant uveal melanomas.

pmc-12727906.title: Exploring the Mahuang Fuzi Xixin Decoction’s mechanism for treating Alzheimer’s disease using molecular docking and network pharmacology
pmc-12727906.creator: Che Chen, Qianfeng Shao, Sheng Zhou
pmc-12727906.description: ObjectiveExplore the potential mechanism of Mahuang Fuzi Xixin Decoction (MFXD) in the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) using network pharmacology, molecular docking approaches, and test its efficacy by in vitro experiments.MethodsActive components of MFXD were screened from TCMSP, BATMAN-TCM, and TCMID, with corresponding targets obtained from SwissTargetPrediction and TCMSP. AD-related differential genes were retrieved from GEO.

pmc-12784732.title: The Prognostic and Predictive Value of Body Mass Index in Patients with HR+/HER2− Breast Cancer Treated with CDK4/6 Inhibitors: A Systematic Literature Review
pmc-12784732.creator: Larisa Maria Badau, Cristina Marinela Oprean, Andrei Dorin Ciocoiu, Paul Epure, Brigitha Vlaicu
pmc-12784732.description: Simple SummaryThis systematic review evaluated the association between BMI and clinical outcomes in patients with HR+/HER2− MBC receiving CDK4/6i. The 14 eligible studies yielded heterogenous results; while several investigations identified a prognostic advantage for overweight or obese patients, others failed to demonstrate a significant predictive correlation between BMI and survival outcomes.

pmc-13233268.title: Primary intracranial myxopapillary ependymoma: two case reports and literature review
pmc-13233268.creator: Lan Zhong, Zhen Xu, Shiyuan Yin, Hongjuan Tian, Feizhou Du, Chuande Zhang, Yihua Chen, Chao Wang
pmc-13233268.description: Myxopapillary ependymoma (MPE), a histological variant of ependymoma, is characterized by a radial arrangement of spindled or epithelioid tumor cells surrounding blood vessels, accompanied by perivascular myxoid changes and microcyst formation. MPE typically occurs in young adults, predominantly in the conus medullaris, cauda equina, and filum terminale.

pmc-13271356.title: Safety and immunogenicity of a booster dose of COVAC-2, a Sepivac SWE™ adjuvanted SARS-CoV-2 recombinant protein vaccine in previously vaccinated healthy adults; a randomized controlled multicentre trial
pmc-13271356.creator: Glenn Hamonic, Supriya Arora, Ravendra Garg, Erin Scruten, Rachelle Buchanan, Stephanie L. Saundh, Nicolas Collin, Stephen Sanche, Noah Vale, Timothy Salter, Scott A. Halperin, Joanne M. Langley, Volker Gerdts, Trina Racine

pmc-13518406.title: Naïve adaptive immune receptor repertoires in celiac disease assessed by machine learning; impact of the HLA-DQ2.5 allotype on the TCR repertoire
pmc-13518406.creator: Aengus Officer, Ida Lindeman, Milena Pavlovic, Christin Lund-Andersen, Eivind Ness-Jensen, Geir Kjetil Sandve, Ludvig M Sollid
pmc-13518406.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The adaptive immune receptor repertoire (AIRR) - the collection of an individual’s B-cell and T-cell receptors (BCRs and TCRs, respectively) - encodes cumulative immune history and is shaped by both germline genetics and environmental exposures. Skewed repertoires have been linked to infections, vaccination responses and autoimmune diseases such as celiac disease (CeD) where biased usage of immunoglobulin and T-cell receptor genes reactive to disease relevant antigens has been reported.

pmc-13584807.title: Bipolar Androgen Therapy as a Potential Mechanistic Bridge to Enhance PARP Inhibitor Efficacy in Prostate Cancer
pmc-13584807.creator: Jhen‐Hao Jhan, Jiun‐Hung Geng, Hung‐Lung Ke, Shu‐Pin Huang, Li Jia
pmc-13584807.description: Prostate cancer remains a leading cause of cancer‐related mortality, largely driven by progression to metastatic castration‐resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). Although poly(ADP‐ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPis) have improved outcomes in patients with homologous recombination repair (HRR) alterations, particularly in BRCA2‐mutated disease, their clinical benefit is limited by restricted patient selection, modest efficacy in non‐BRCA HRR alterations, and the frequent emergence of resistance.
